content: A dermatosis is a broad term used in medicine to describe any disease of the skin. The plural form of the term is dermatoses. It is important to differentiate dermatosis from dermatitis, as the latter specifically refers to inflammation of the skin. While dermatitis is a subset of dermatoses characterized by inflammatory symptoms, not all dermatoses involve inflammation. Dermatoses encompass a wide range of skin diseases, many of which are non-contagious. Certain systemic diseases, such as measles and rubella, can manifest symptoms on the skin, but these conditions are not classified as dermatoses. Examples of skin diseases that fall under the category of dermatoses include skin cancer, eczema, psoriasis, acne, impetigo, scabies, sunburn, warts, fifth disease (also known as erythema infectiosum or slapped face disease), tinea, herpes, ulcers, and pruritus. Some skin disorders may result from the absorption of harmful substances through the skin. Here is a comprehensive list of skin diseases that are classified as dermatoses: Acne: A common skin condition involving clogged hair follicles, leading to pimples, blackheads, or cysts. Actinic keratosis: Angioma: A benign growth of blood vessels in the skin. Athlete's foot: A fungal infection affecting the skin of the feet. Aquagenic pruritus: Intense itching triggered by contact with water. Argyria: A condition caused by silver accumulation in the skin, leading to a bluish-gray discoloration. Atopic dermatitis: A chronic inflammatory skin condition characterized by itching and eczema-like lesions. Baldness: The loss of hair, often due to genetic or hormonal factors. Basal cell carcinoma: A type of skin cancer originating in the basal cells of the epidermis. Bed sore: Behcet's disease: A rare inflammatory disorder causing ulcers and skin lesions. Blepharitis: Inflammation of the eyelids, often associated with redness and crusting. Boil: A painful, pus-filled infection of a hair follicle or oil gland. Bowen's disease: A form of early-stage skin cancer presenting as scaly patches. Bullous pemphigoid: An autoimmune disorder causing large, fluid-filled blisters. Canker sore: Painful ulcers that develop inside the mouth. Carbuncles: Clusters of boils caused by bacterial infection. Cellulitis: A bacterial skin infection characterized by redness, swelling, and warmth. Chloracne: Chronic dermatitis of the hands and feet: Persistent inflammation of the skin on the hands and feet. Cold sores: Blisters caused by the herpes simplex virus, typically around the mouth. Contact dermatitis: Skin inflammation caused by contact with irritants or allergens, such as poison ivy. Creeping eruption: A skin condition caused by hookworm larvae migrating under the skin. Dandruff: Flaking of the scalp due to seborrheic dermatitis or other causes. Dermatitis: A general term for skin inflammation, often accompanied by redness and itching. Dermatitis herpetiformis: A chronic, intensely itchy rash associated with celiac disease. Dermatofibroma: A benign skin growth, often firm and raised. Diaper rash: Dyshidrosis: A type of eczema causing small, itchy blisters on the hands and feet. Eczema: A chronic skin condition characterized by inflammation, redness, and itching. Epidermolysis bullosa: A group of genetic disorders causing fragile skin and blistering. Erysipelas: A bacterial skin infection causing raised, red, and swollen areas. Erythroderma: Widespread redness and scaling of the skin, often due to underlying conditions. Friction blister: Genital wart: A sexually transmitted infection caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV). Gestational pemphigoid: A rare autoimmune blistering disorder occurring during pregnancy. Grover's disease: A transient skin condition causing itchy red spots, often on the chest or back. Hemangioma: A benign tumor of blood vessels, often appearing as a red birthmark. Hidradenitis suppurativa: A chronic inflammatory condition causing painful lumps under the skin. Hives: Raised, itchy welts on the skin, often due to an allergic reaction. Hyperhidrosis: Excessive sweating beyond normal physiological needs. Ichthyosis: A group of disorders causing dry, scaly skin. Impetigo: A contagious bacterial skin infection causing sores and crusting. Jock itch: A fungal infection affecting the groin area. Kaposi's sarcoma: A cancerous condition involving abnormal growth of blood vessels, often associated with HIV/AIDS. Keloid: An overgrowth of scar tissue at the site of a skin injury. Keratoacanthoma: A rapidly growing skin tumor that may resemble squamous cell carcinoma. Keratosis pilaris: A common condition causing rough, bumpy skin, often on the arms or thighs. Lewandowsky-Lutz dysplasia: A rare genetic disorder causing tree-like growths on the skin. Lice infection: Infestation of the skin or hair by lice. Lichen planus: An inflammatory condition causing flat, purple, itchy lesions. Lichen simplex chronicus: Thickened, itchy skin caused by chronic scratching or rubbing. Lipoma: A benign tumor of fatty tissue under the skin. Lymphadenitis: Inflammation of lymph nodes, often due to infection. Malignant melanoma: A dangerous form of skin cancer arising from melanocytes. Melasma: Dark, patchy discoloration of the skin, often due to hormonal changes. Miliaria: Heat rash caused by blocked sweat ducts. Molluscum contagiosum: A viral skin infection causing small, raised, and painless bumps. Nummular dermatitis: A type of eczema presenting as coin-shaped patches on the skin. Paget's disease of the nipple: A rare form of breast cancer involving the skin of the nipple. Pediculosis: Infestation of the skin or hair by lice. Pemphigus: A group of autoimmune disorders causing blistering of the skin and mucous membranes. Perioral dermatitis: A rash around the mouth, often caused by topical steroids or irritants. Photoallergy: Photosensitivity: Increased sensitivity of the skin to sunlight. Pityriasis rosea: A self-limiting rash often starting with a single herald patch. Pityriasis rubra pilaris: A rare skin disorder causing scaling and redness. Porphyria: A group of disorders affecting the skin and nervous system, often triggered by sunlight. Psoriasis: A chronic autoimmune condition causing red, scaly patches on the skin. Raynaud's disease: A condition causing reduced blood flow to the extremities, leading to discoloration. Ringworm: A fungal infection causing circular, red, and scaly patches on the skin. Rosacea: A chronic skin condition causing redness and visible blood vessels on the face. Scabies: A contagious skin infestation caused by mites. Scleroderma: A connective tissue disorder causing thickened, hardened skin. Scrofula: A form of tuberculosis affecting the lymph nodes, often with skin involvement. Sebaceous cyst: A noncancerous lump under the skin filled with sebum. Seborrheic keratosis: A benign skin growth with a waxy or stuck-on appearance. Seborrhoeic dermatitis: A chronic inflammatory condition causing flaky, greasy scales. Shingles: A painful rash caused by reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus. Skin cancer: A group of cancers arising from skin cells, including basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and melanoma. Skin tags: Small, benign growths of skin, often in areas of friction. Spider veins: Small, dilated blood vessels visible on the skin's surface. Squamous cell carcinoma: A type of skin cancer arising from squamous cells in the epidermis. Stasis dermatitis: Skin inflammation caused by poor circulation, often in the lower legs. Sunburn: Tick bite: A skin reaction caused by the bite of a tick, potentially transmitting diseases. Tinea barbae: A fungal infection of the beard area. Tinea capitis: A fungal infection of the scalp. Tinea corporis: A fungal infection of the body, also known as ringworm. Tinea cruris: A fungal infection of the groin, also known as jock itch. Tinea pedis: A fungal infection of the feet, also known as athlete's foot. Tinea unguium: A fungal infection of the nails. Tinea versicolor: A fungal infection causing discolored patches on the skin. Tungiasis: A parasitic skin infestation caused by sand fleas. Urticaria (Hives): Raised, itchy welts on the skin, often due to an allergic reaction. Vagabond's disease: A skin condition caused by chronic lice infestation. Vitiligo: A condition causing loss of skin pigmentation in patches. Warts: Benign growths caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV). Wheal (Weal or Welt): A raised, red, and itchy area of skin, often due to an allergic reaction.
